speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask a few clarifying questions to assess this newborn's condition. How old is the baby in days, and has the vomiting been green or bile-stained? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound to rule out intestinal obstruction.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia (likely Duodenal). The bilious vomiting, feeding intolerance, and onset within the first day of life in a newborn with no fever are classic for a mechanical bowel obstruction like intestinal atresia. The requested abdominal ultrasound is critical to confirm the "double bubble" sign or identify a distal obstruction.
